docs.title: Welcome to Fivemon
docs.text:
Fivemon is a comprehensive mod/resource set for FiveM, featuring a custom framework at its core called uri-core. This state-of-the-art framework is highly optimized and offers a wide array of customization options, easy translation, and seamless content addition through simple files or even its own custom language, .uri. This language allows developers to create advanced NPCs, quests, and logic-rich gameplay elements to enhance the player experience. Fivemon is also equipped with a powerful Monster mechanics addon, supporting an advanced battle simulator.

In the Fivemon Wiki, you'll be able to dive into learning .uri starting with the introduction. In guides, you can explore various topics to help you learn or better understand different aspects of the framework. In the core and monsters sections, you'll find up to four main categories: resources, extensions, and utilities. In resources, you'll have access to several repositories containing server content, such as items, Monster, abilities, and more. The extensions section provides additional functionalities for .uri, including new actions and constructors. Finally, in utilities, you'll find commands, configuration files, and control schemes to manage and customize your experience.

Explore this page to discover all the exciting features Fivemon has to offer.

docs.title: Monster Team
docs.text:
Each player has access to an advanced Monster team, allowing them to easily view and manage their team. The interface is user-friendly, offering a clear view of each Monster's stats, abilities, and moves.

Fivemon includes all the essential mechanics needed for modern Monster gameplay, including stats like EVs, IVs, natures, and abilities. Monster can evolve, level up, and participate in complex battles, all within a flexible and immersive system.

docs.title: Monster PC
docs.text: Players can also utilize a fully configurable PC system with filters to help organize and search for Monster. For example, you can filter Monster based on whether they can learn a specific TM, change box colors, and much more.

docs.title: Monster Interactions
docs.text: Players can carry their Monster and interact with them organically by throwing them out, recalling them, or having them follow in a natural, fluid manner.

docs.title: Advanced Spawn System
docs.text: Fivemon's spawn system is highly configurable, determining which Monster appear in each area based on biomes, time of day, weather conditions, and rarity tiers. This makes rare Monster encounters even more special and exciting.

docs.title: Monsterdex
docs.text: Players have access to a Monsterdex, allowing them to track their progress as trainers. They can use the Monsterdex to capture information using the in-game camera or their Monster list. The Monsterdex provides valuable insights into their journey.

docs.title: Skins for Monster
docs.text: Fivemon introduces a unique system for custom Monster skins, allowing players to customize their Monster and enhance their connection with their team. This feature adds a personal touch, making the gameplay experience even more rewarding.

docs.title: Flexible Battle System
docs.text:
The battle system in Fivemon is extremely flexible, allowing for a variety of battle formats. You can have battles with up to four teams, and each team can have up to six Monster. This means you can create battles like 2v2, 3v3, or even free-for-alls like 1v1v1v1. The possibilities are endless. NPCs, wild Monster, mission Monster, or players can all participate in battles.

The battle interface is user-friendly, showing all the relevant information needed to manage the battle. Additionally, spectators can watch battles by simply standing near them, encouraging player interaction.

docs.title: Gym Badges
docs.text: Fivemon includes a Gym and Badge system, where players can take on Gym Leaders and collect badges as they work towards becoming the Champion. This structured challenge adds a competitive layer to the experience, motivating players to rise through the ranks.

docs.title: Customization for Playmakers
docs.text: Fivemon offers a wide range of commands for playmakers to customize the experience. Whether it’s creating custom Monster, designing new items like custom potions or Monster balls, or setting up unique zones that only players with specific qualifications can access, the possibilities are endless.

docs.title: Custom Zones
docs.text: You can create zones that only trainers with certain achievements or levels can enter. For example, you might have a special area for players above level 50 where rare and powerful Monster appear.

docs.title: Custom Achievements
docs.text: You can also define achievements for players, such as defeating 50 wild Monster or completing the Monsterdex. These achievements can be tied to zones, creating a progression system that rewards dedicated players.

docs.title: Custom Content
docs.text: Using .uri, you can create custom NPCs with personalized dialogues and behaviors. For instance, you could design an evil duo that blocks access to a specific area until they are defeated in a 2v2 battle. You can even create raid battles with Monster levels over 1000, encouraging community teamwork to achieve a shared goal.

docs.title: Monster Skills
docs.text: In Fivemon, your Monster aren't just battle companions—they can also assist you in exploring the world in exciting ways. You can fly through the skies on the back of a flying-type Monster, surf across the water, or even dive into the depths with a water-type. Additionally, with certain Monster have the ability to ride them or you can carry them.

docs.title: Trading System
docs.text: In Fivemon, trading is a vital part of your journey. You can trade Monsters and items with other players to complete your collection, strengthen your team, or just help a friend in need. Whether you're exchanging rare creatures or valuable gear, trading creates a dynamic economy and encourages collaboration between trainers.

docs.title: Farming Zones
docs.text: Fivemon lets you customize your experience by creating farming zones—special areas where specific Monsters appear more frequently. Whether you're looking to train your team, gather crafting materials, or hunt rare spawns, farming zones give you control over your grind. These zones can be tailored to fit your playstyle and resource needs.

docs.title: Core Framework Features
docs.text:
Beyond the Monster content, uri-core provides a powerful framework with features such as:

  • A custom loading screen that displays user information.
  • A custom character loading system.
  • An advanced inventory system with window-based navigation.
  • A pause/personal menu that centralizes everything a player needs to navigate the world easily. Organizations, quests, quest group, settings...

docs.title: Endless Possibilities
docs.text:
Fivemon gives you all the tools to create your own world. Whether you want to develop an advanced Monster ecosystem, build a thriving player community, or design intricate NPC interactions, Fivemon is here to help you achieve it. The only limit is your imagination.

What are you waiting for? Join us on Discord!

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Name Type Description Possibilities ask interaction Presents a question to the player with a set of possible responses. The result is the index of the chosen response. 2 beRescued behaviour Allows an NPC to be rescued by a player. The NPC will follow the player to a specified rescue position. 3 blockForceInteraction interaction Blocks an NPC from forcing an interaction with a specific character. 1 clear both Stops the NPC from performing any current tasks or animations. 1 combat behaviour Engages the NPC in combat with a specified target. 2 combatClosestPlayer behaviour Engages the NPC in combat with the closest player within a specified distance. 2 command interaction Executes a specified command on the client side. 1 cower both Makes the NPC cower in fear. 1 dice both Rolls a dice with the specified number of faces and returns a random result. 1 distanceCoordsClose both Checks if the NPC is within a specified distance from a given set of coordinates. 2 distanceEntityClose both Checks if the NPC is within a specified distance from a given entity. 2 do both Executes a behaviour tree. 1 driveToCoords behaviour Makes the NPC drive a vehicle to the specified coordinates. 2 driveToEntity behaviour Makes the NPC drive a vehicle towards a specified entity. 2 enterClosestVehicle behaviour Makes the NPC enter the closest vehicle within a specified distance. 3 enterVehicle behaviour Makes the NPC enter a specified vehicle. 2 flee behaviour Makes the NPC flee from a specified pedestrian if they are within a certain distance. 2 fleeCoords behaviour Makes the NPC flee from specified coordinates if they are within a certain distance. 2 forceInteraction behaviour Forces an interaction between the NPC and a nearby player. If blockForceInteraction has been used on a player, the NPC won't interact with that player until unblockForceInteraction is used. 2 getClosestPlayer behaviour Finds the closest player to the NPC within a specified distance and stores the player entity in a global variable. 2 getClosestVehicle behaviour Finds the closest vehicle to the NPC within a specified distance, optionally filtered by model and flag, and stores the vehicle entity in a global variable. 1 getCombatTarget behaviour Retrieves the NPC's current melee combat target and stores the target entity in a global variable. 2 getGlobalState both Retrieves a global state associated with the NPC and stores it in a global variable within the behavior tree." 1 getLocalState interaction Retrieves a local state associated with the NPC and the specific player, then stores it in a local variable within the behavior tree. 1 getNPC both Retrieves an NPC by its ID from the NPC repository and stores it in a global variable. 2 give interaction Gives a specified item and quantity from the NPC to the character. 2 giveUbication interaction Sets a new waypoint on the map at the specified coordinates. 1 globalCheck both Checks if a global state for the NPC is already marked. If not marked, it sets the state and returns 1; if already marked, it returns 2. 2 goToClosestPlayer behaviour Makes the NPC move towards the closest player within a specified distance and speed. 3 goToCoords behaviour Makes the NPC move towards the specified coordinates. 2 goToEntity behaviour Makes the NPC move towards a specified entity within a given distance and speed. 2 goToEntityOffset behaviour Makes the NPC move to a position offset from a specified entity by a given X and Y distance. 2 hasQuestCompleted interaction Checks if the character has completed a quest. 2 hasQuestStarted interaction Checks if the character has started a quest. 2 if both Evaluates a given value as a condition and returns a result based on whether the value is true or false. 2 input interaction Prompts the player to input a text value, which is then stored in a local variable. 2 knows interaction Checks if the NPC recognizes or knows the character. 2 localCheck interaction Checks if a local state for the NPC related to a specific player is already marked. If not marked, it sets the state and returns 1; if already marked, it returns 2. 2 log both Logs a message to the client's debug console. 1 lookCoords behaviour Makes the NPC turn to face a specific set of coordinates. 2 lookEntity behaviour Makes the NPC turn to face a specified entity. 2 me interaction Displays an action message from the NPC in the chat, typically used for roleplaying purposes. 1 nothing both Does nothing. 1 openCraftingTable interaction Opens a specified crafting table interface for the player. 1 openShop interaction Opens a specified shop interface for the player. 1 openStorage interaction Opens a specified storage interface for the player. 1 playAnimation behaviour Plays a specified animation on the NPC. 2 playingAnimation condition Checks if the NPC is currently playing a specified animation. 2 remove interaction Removes a specified item and quantity from the NPC to the character. 2 return both Ends the current action sequence and returns a specified result. 1 serverLog both Logs a message to the server console with the 'Action' tag for debugging purposes. 1 set both Sets multiple global variables within the behavior tree. 1 setCoords behaviour Sets the NPC's position to the specified coordinates. 2 setGlobalState both Sets a global state for the NPC. 1 setLocalState interaction Sets a local state for the NPC related to a specific player. 1 setWalk behaviour Sets the NPC's walking style to the specified animation set. 1 showPicture interaction Displays a picture. 1 spawnVehicle interaction Spawns a vehicle in the specified position. 3 startQuest interaction Initiates a quest for the NPC. This action handles starting, rewarding, or failing the quest depending on the player's progress. 7 surround behaviour Positions the NPC around a specified entity, calculating an offset based on the number of people surrounding and the NPC's position among them. 1 teleport behaviour Teleports the NPC to the specified entity if the entity is not within a certain distance. 2 tell interaction Displays a message to the player from the NPC. 1 unblockForceInteraction interaction Allows an NPC to force an interaction with a specific character again by unblocking it. 1 wait behaviour Pauses the NPC's behaviour for a specified duration. 2 wander behaviour Makes the NPC wander within a specified area, randomly moving around a central point. 1

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Presents a question to the player with a set of possible responses. The result is the index of the chosen response.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 title string Yes The question or title to be presented to the player. No 2 answer string Yes The possible responses to the question. The number of responses is optional. Yes

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The index of the selected response. 2 If the player cancels, the result is the index after the last option.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name NPC 
  model a_m_m_eastsa_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    ask "What will you do?" Fight Run 
      tell "You chose to fight." 
      tell "You chose to run." 

  behaviour 
    nothing

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Allows an NPC to be rescued by a player. The NPC will follow the player to a specified rescue position.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 x number Yes The X coordinate of the rescue position. No 2 y number Yes The Y coordinate of the rescue position. No 3 z number Yes The Z coordinate of the rescue position. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 1 if the NPC is already at the rescue position. 2 2 if the NPC is following the player. 3 3 if the NPC is waiting where they are.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Hostage 
  model a_m_m_farmer_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    beRescued 100.0 200.0 300.0

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Blocks an NPC from forcing an interaction with a specific character.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
interaction 
    blockForceInteraction 
      tell "This NPC can no longer force interactions with you." 

  behaviour 
    nothing

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Stops the NPC from performing any current tasks or animations.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Guard 
  model s_m_m_security_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    clear

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Engages the NPC in combat with a specified target.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 target Entity Yes The target that the NPC will engage in combat. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The target is already dead. 2 The NPC engages in combat with the target.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Enemy 
  model g_m_y_ballaorig_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    getClosestPlayer player 10 
      combat $player

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Engages the NPC in combat with the closest player within a specified distance.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 distance number No The maximum distance within which the NPC will engage the closest player. Defaults to 15 if not specified. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The NPC engages in combat with the closest player. 2 No player is within the specified distance, or the NPC cannot engage.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Guard 
  model s_m_y_cop_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    combatClosestPlayer 20

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Executes a specified command on the client side.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 command string Yes The command to be executed. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The command has been executed.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
interaction 
    command "me stares intently" 

  behaviour 
    nothing

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Civilian 
  model a_f_m_skidrow_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    cower

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Rolls a dice with the specified number of faces and returns a random result.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 faces integer Yes The number of faces on the dice. Accepts any positive integer. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The result of the dice roll, a random number between 1 and the specified number of faces.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
interaction 
    dice 4 
      tell "You rolled the number 1." 
      tell "You rolled the number 2." 
      tell "You rolled the number 3." 
      tell "You rolled the number 4." 

  behaviour 
    nothing

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Checks if the NPC is within a specified distance from a given set of coordinates.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 distance number Yes The maximum distance within which the NPC should be to return a positive result. No 2 x number Yes The X coordinate to check against. No 3 y number Yes The Y coordinate to check against. No 4 z number Yes The Z coordinate to check against. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The NPC is within the specified distance. 2 The NPC is not within the specified distance.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Guard 
  model s_m_m_security_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    distanceCoordsClose 5.0 100.0 200.0 300.0 
      tell "The NPC is close to the specified location." 
      tell "The NPC is not close to the specified location." 

  behaviour 
    nothing

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Checks if the NPC is within a specified distance from a given entity.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 distance number Yes The maximum distance within which the NPC should be to return a positive result. No 2 entity Entity Yes The entity to check the distance against. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The NPC is within the specified distance from the entity. 2 The NPC is not within the specified distance from the entity.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Guard 
  model s_m_y_cop_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    getClosestPlayer player 10 
      distanceEntityClose 5.0 player 
        tell "The NPC is close to the player." 
        tell "The NPC is not close enough to the player."

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 behaviour BehaviourID Yes The ID of the behaviour tree to execute. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The last node result in the behaviour tree.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
BEHAVIOURTREE 

  name example_behaviour 

  interaction 
    tell "Hi, how are you?" 

  NPC 

  name NPC_1 
  model a_m_m_eastsa_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    do example_behaviour

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Makes the NPC drive a vehicle to the specified coordinates.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 vehicle Vehicle Yes The vehicle the NPC will drive. No 2 x number Yes The X coordinate to drive to. No 3 y number Yes The Y coordinate to drive to. No 4 z number Yes The Z coordinate to drive to. No 5 distance number No The stopping distance from the coordinates. Defaults to 10.0 if not specified. No 6 speed number No The speed at which the NPC should drive. Defaults to 26.0 if not specified. No 7 mode number No The driving mode to use. Defaults to 786468 if not specified. https://vespura.com/fivem/drivingstyle/ No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The NPC is already within the specified distance from the coordinates. 2 The NPC driving to the specified coordinates.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Driver 
  model s_m_y_cop_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    getClosestVehicle vehicle 
      driveToCoords $vehicle 150.0 200.0 300.0

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Makes the NPC drive a vehicle towards a specified entity.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 vehicle Vehicle Yes The vehicle the NPC will drive. No 2 entity Entity Yes The entity to which the NPC will drive. No 3 distance number No The stopping distance from the entity. Defaults to 10.0 if not specified. No 4 speed number No The speed at which the NPC should drive. Defaults to 26.0 if not specified. No 5 mode number No The driving mode to use. Defaults to 786468 if not specified. See more details at https://vespura.com/fivem/drivingstyle/ No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The NPC is already within the specified distance from the entity. 2 The NPC starts driving towards the entity.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name TaxiDriver 
  model s_m_m_taxidriver_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    getClosestPlayer player 
      getClosestVehicle vehicle 
        driveToEntity $vehicle $player

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Makes the NPC enter the closest vehicle within a specified distance.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 vehicle Entity Yes The global variable name where the vehicle entity will be stored. No 2 distance number Yes The maximum distance within which the NPC should look for a vehicle. No 3 seatIndex number No The seat index the NPC should attempt to enter. Defaults to the driver's seat if not specified. No 4 speed number No The speed at which the NPC should enter the vehicle. Defaults to 2.0 if not specified. No 5 timeout number No The time in milliseconds to wait before giving up on entering the vehicle. Defaults to -1 (no timeout) if not specified. No 6 mode number No The mode of entry. Defaults to 1 if not specified. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The NPC is already in or entering a vehicle. 2 The NPC starts entering the closest vehicle. 3 No vehicle was found within the specified distance.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Thief 
  model a_m_y_hipster_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    enterClosestVehicle myVehicle 15.0 0 2.0 -1 1

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Makes the NPC enter a specified vehicle.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 vehicle Vehicle Yes The vehicle that the NPC will enter. No 2 seatIndex number No The seat index the NPC should attempt to enter. Defaults to -1 (any seat) if not specified. No 3 speed number No The speed at which the NPC should enter the vehicle. Defaults to 2.0 if not specified. No 4 timeout number No The time in milliseconds to wait before giving up on entering the vehicle. Defaults to -1 (no timeout) if not specified. No 5 mode number No The mode of entry. Defaults to 1 if not specified. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The NPC is already in or entering the specified vehicle. 2 The NPC starts entering the specified vehicle.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Driver 
  model s_m_y_cop_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    enterVehicle myVehicle -1 2.0 -1 1

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Makes the NPC flee from a specified pedestrian if they are within a certain distance.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 ped Ped Yes The pedestrian from whom the NPC will flee. No 2 distance number No The distance within which the NPC will start fleeing. Defaults to 200.0 if not specified. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The NPC is already within the specified distance from the pedestrian and is fleeing. 2 The NPC starts fleeing from the pedestrian.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Coward 
  model a_m_y_hipster_02 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    flee player 150.0

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Makes the NPC flee from specified coordinates if they are within a certain distance.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 x number Yes The X coordinate from which the NPC will flee. No 2 y number Yes The Y coordinate from which the NPC will flee. No 3 z number Yes The Z coordinate from which the NPC will flee. No 4 distance number No The distance within which the NPC will start fleeing. Defaults to 200.0 if not specified. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The NPC is already within the specified distance from the coordinates and is fleeing. 2 The NPC starts fleeing from the specified coordinates.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Runner 
  model a_m_y_runner_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Forces an interaction between the NPC and a nearby player. If blockForceInteraction has been used on a player, the NPC won't interact with that player until unblockForceInteraction is used.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The interaction was not successful. 2 The interaction was successful.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name AggressiveNPC 
  model s_m_y_dealer_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    tell "Hey, you!" 

  behaviour 
    forceInteraction

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Finds the closest player to the NPC within a specified distance and stores the player entity in a global variable.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 player Entity Yes The global variable name where the player entity will be stored. No 2 distance number No The maximum distance to search for a player. Defaults to 200 if not specified. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The closest player was found and stored in the global variable. 2 No player was found within the specified distance.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Watcher 
  model s_m_m_security_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    getClosestPlayer closestPlayer 15

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Finds the closest vehicle to the NPC within a specified distance, optionally filtered by model and flag, and stores the vehicle entity in a global variable.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 vehicle Entity Yes The global variable name where the vehicle entity will be stored. No 2 distance number Yes The maximum distance to search for a vehicle. No 3 model string No The model of the vehicle to filter the search. If not specified, any model is accepted. No 4 flag number No An optional flag to further filter the vehicle search. Defaults to 0 if not specified. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The closest vehicle was found and stored in the global variable.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Driver 
  model s_m_y_cop_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    getClosestVehicle closestVehicle 1000

docs.text: Retrieves the NPC's current melee combat target and stores the target entity in a global variable.

docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 target Entity Yes The global variable name where the combat target entity will be stored. No

docs.title: Example

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Retrieves a global state associated with the NPC and stores it in a global variable within the behavior tree."

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 k string Yes The key of the global state to retrieve. No 2 output string Yes The name of the global variable where the retrieved state will be stored. No 3 npc NPCID No Optional NPC id No

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
interaction 
    getGlobalState npc_hapiness npc_hapiness 
      tell "Im like $npc_hapiness% happy." 

  behaviour 
    nothing

docs.text: Retrieves a local state associated with the NPC and the specific player, then stores it in a local variable within the behavior tree.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 k string Yes The key of the local state to retrieve. No 2 output string Yes The name of the local variable where the retrieved state will be stored. No 3 npc NPCID No Optional NPC id No

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
interaction 
    getLocalState npc_relationship player_relationship 
      tell "Your relationship with this NPC is $player_relationship." 

  behaviour 
    nothing

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Retrieves an NPC by its ID from the NPC repository and stores it in a global variable.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 name NPC Yes The global variable name where the retrieved NPC will be stored. No 2 id string Yes The unique identifier of the NPC to retrieve. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The NPC was found and stored in the global variable. 2 The NPC with the specified ID was not found.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Helper 
  model s_m_m_paramedic_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    getNPC helperNPC npc_id_example

docs.title: Description

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Checks if a global state for the NPC is already marked. If not marked, it sets the state and returns 1; if already marked, it returns 2.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 k string Yes The key of the global state to check or set. No 2 npc NPCID No Optional NPC id No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The global state was not marked and has been set. 2 The global state was already marked.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
interaction 
    globalCheck quest_started 
      tell "The quest has just been marked as started." 
      tell "The quest was already marked as started." 

  behaviour 
    nothing

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Makes the NPC move towards the closest player within a specified distance and speed.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 distance number No The maximum distance to search for a player. Defaults to 15 if not specified. No 2 speed number No The speed at which the NPC should move towards the player. Defaults to 2.0 if not specified. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The NPC is in player's proximity. 2 The NPC moves towards the closest player. 3 No player was found within the specified distance.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Follower 
  model s_m_m_security_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    goToClosestPlayer 15 3.0

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Makes the NPC move towards the specified coordinates.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 x number Yes The X coordinate to move to. No 2 y number Yes The Y coordinate to move to. No 3 z number Yes The Z coordinate to move to. No 4 distance number No The stopping distance from the coordinates. If specified and the NPC is within this distance, the action will not move the NPC. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The NPC is already within the specified distance from the coordinates. 2 The NPC is moving towards the specified coordinates.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Walker 
  model s_m_m_security_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    goToCoords 150.0 200.0 300.0 10.0

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Makes the NPC move towards a specified entity within a given distance and speed.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 entity Entity Yes The entity that the NPC will move towards. No 2 distance number No The distance at which the NPC will stop moving towards the entity. Defaults to 2.0 if not specified. No 3 speed number No The speed at which the NPC should move towards the entity. Defaults to 2.0 if not specified. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The NPC is already within the specified distance from the entity. 2 The NPC is moving towards the entity.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Follower 
  model s_m_y_cop_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Makes the NPC move to a position offset from a specified entity by a given X and Y distance.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 entity Entity Yes The entity relative to which the NPC will move. No 2 x number Yes The X offset from the entity's position. No 3 y number Yes The Y offset from the entity's position. No 4 relative boolean No Whether the offset is relative to the entity's heading. Defaults to false if not specified. No

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: # Description 1 The NPC is already within the specified offset distance from the entity. 2 The NPC is moving to the specified offset position relative to the entity.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NPC 

  name Guard 
  model s_m_y_cop_01 
  position -1020.72 4839.78 258.30 0.0 

  interaction 
    nothing 

  behaviour 
    getClosestPlayer player 
      goToEntityOffset $player 5.0 0.0 true

docs.title: Description

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Prompts the player to input a text value, which is then stored in a local variable.

docs.text: # Name Type Mandatory Description Multiple 1 output string Yes The name of the local variable where the player's input will be stored. No 2 text string Yes The text message that prompts the player for input. No 3 placeholder string No The placeholder text that appears in the input field. Optional.       tell "Thank you, $playerName!"

    nothing

Only allowed species can be used, or certain species can be blocked. started_or_completed_quest Allows entry if the player has either started or completed any of the listed quests. started_quest Requires the player to have started one or more specific quests to be allowed inside the zone. types Restricts access based on the types of Pokémon in the player's party. docs.title: Config
docs.text: Name Description Edit config The client and server config. data/config/config.json locales The locales used for the translation. data/locales/xx_XX.json onlyserverconfig The server config. data/config/onlyserverconfig.json

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Description locale The locale of the server. Example: en_US, es_ES, pt_BR, etc. money An object containing configurations for in-game currency. money.name The name of the in-game currency. Example: Pokédollars. money.symbol The symbol of the currency. Example: $, ¥, etc. money.default The default amount of money players start with. start An object containing configurations for player start. start.fastRestart Enables or disables auto select first character. Only recommended for development. start.position The default spawn coordinates for players selecting/creating character(x, y, z). start.heading The default heading or direction the player will face when selecting/creating character. start.spawns A list of initial spawn points with coordinates and heading. status An object containing configurations for player status. status.tick The time interval in ticks to update hunger and thirst. status.increase.probability The probability of hunger or thirst increasing per tick. status.increase.hunger The amount hunger increases each tick. status.increase.thirst The amount thirst increases each tick. status.damage.probability The probability of the player taking damage due to hunger or thirst. status.damage.hunger The amount of damage dealt when hunger is too low. status.damage.thirst The amount of damage dealt when thirst is too low. dead An object containing configurations for player death. dead.time The time (in ticks or seconds) before the player respawns after death. dead.spawns A list of respawn points with coordinates and heading. dni An object containing DNI (ID) for every character. dni.length The length of the generated DNI (ID). dni.preffix The prefix for the DNI (ID). Example: URI-. weather An object containing weather configurations for the server. weather.defaultTime The default in-game time when the server starts (hours, minutes, seconds). weather.defaultWeather The default weather at the start. Example: CLEAR, RAIN, CLOUDS, etc. weather.timeSpeed The speed at which time progresses in the game. weather.weatherChangeTick The time interval in ticks to check for weather changes. weather.changeWeatherProb The probability of changing the weather at each check. weather.changeStageProb The probability of changing the weather stage within the same type. weather.weatherSet A list of weather sets with their probabilities. Example: CLEAR, RAIN, FOGGY, etc. GPS An object containing GPS locations for the server. GPS.name The identifier of the location for GPS purposes. GPS.label The display name for the GPS location. GPS.coords The coordinates (x, y, z) of the GPS location. nui_logging Enables or disables logging for the NUI interface. debug Enables or disables debugging mode. logging An object containing logging configurations for different modules. logging.saveable Enables or disables saving logs to db. logging.printable Enables or disables printing logs to console. tokens An object containing token mappings for different languages for .uri files.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Description localeKey The key is the locale code and the value is the locale name. Use %s for string interpolation. If you want to alternate the order of the arguments, use %s1, %s2, etc. Example: %s1 corresponds to the first argument in the original string.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Description version The version of the server shown in loading screen. identifier The identifier got from fivem for the user id, typically 'discord'. discord An object containing configurations for the Discord integration. discord.token The bot token for the Discord API. discord.guild The ID of the Discord server (guild) where the bot operates. discord.announcements The ID of the channel used for sending announcements. This will be shown in the loading screen. discord.roles An object containing role IDs for the a rol name. discord.whitelist_roles Roles that grant whitelist access to the server. discord.queue_roles The queue priority roles from lowest to highest. discord.verified_roles The roles that mark a user as verified. discord.admin_roles Roles that grant full administrative access to the server. restart An object containing configurations for server restarts. restart.times Times at which the server will automatically restart. Must be the same as TxAdmin. From lower to higher. Format: HH:MM. restart.notify Times (in minutes) to notify players before the server restarts. Example: [1, 5, 15, 30]. logging An object containing logging configurations for different modules. logging.saveable Enables or disables saving logs to db. logging.printable Enables or disables printing logs to console. logging.webhook The webhook URL for sending logs to a Discord channel.
